solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Standard form filled with rubbish automatically?

indicators.note: a thing filled with something has that something packed inside it, here between its two parts

parts.note: par is the standard score, as in golf
to fashion is to form or shape
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A standard official form has been filled in with nonsense without anyone thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR and FASHION together make the 'standard form', and ROT is stuffed between them to give PARROT-FASHION.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating parrot-fashion means by rote without understanding, mechanically, which the question mark flags as a loose equivalent of automatically.

clue.text: Mineral mixture in ewer falling short

indicators.note: in means the mixture goes inside the shortened jug
falling short means the word for ewer stops before its final letter

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug, a pitcher
a blend is a mixture

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: some mineral blend poured into a jug that is slightly too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mineral mixture' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Mineral'; 'mixture' supplies the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchblende is a uranium-rich ore, a mineral source of radium and uranium.

clue.text: Got it right about work coming up

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: Someone got the sums right after their work went up.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands alone; RE and GO are reversed together to give OGER, so R + OGER = ROGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is the radio operator's acknowledgement meaning message received and understood.

clue.text: Hotel specialist tipped to administer leaderless institution

indicators.note: tipped means the hotel and specialist letters are tipped over, read backwards

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pro is an expert or specialist

indicators.note: leaderless means the word for administer loses its first letter

parts.note: to manage is to administer

explanation.surface: A hotel expert has been tipped off to run an institution that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' acts on both hotel and specialist together, so the letter for Hotel ends up last of the four.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a residential institution caring for children without parents.

clue.text: Guy coming into Algarve resort brings hash

indicators.note: something coming into a place enters it, so this word goes inside the other

parts.note: Faro is the main town of Portugal's Algarve coast
to guy someone is to mock them, as is to rag

explanation.surface: A man arriving at a Portuguese beach resort brings cannabis with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man, but here it is the verb to tease; 'hash' reads as the drug, but means a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or mixture, and to make a hash of something is to produce such a muddle.

clue.text: Flavoursome addition to food — and booze!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a liquid served with a dish to add flavour
second meaning: slang for alcoholic drink, as in being on the hard stuff

explanation.walkthrough: The dash and exclamation make it read like a menu adding a drink; 'hitting the sauce' means drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a liquid condiment poured over dishes and is also informal slang for alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: Groom to struggle with libido leaving party in confusion

indicators.note: to struggle is to thrash about, so these letters are thrown around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaving means the party goes out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A bridegroom fights his sex drive and quits the celebration, bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBIDO loses DO to leave LIBI, and GROOM with LIBI is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a complicated, muddled situation, a tangle of affairs.

clue.text: Fancy pigeon Greek character needed on top

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of needed

explanation.surface: A showy bird apparently needs a Greek letter added to it.
explanation.walkthrough: A fancy pigeon is a breed kept for show; the nun is one such breed, named for its hood-like markings.
explanation.definitionFit: The nun is a recognised breed of fancy pigeon with a veil-like crest resembling a nun's headdress.

clue.text: One does associate with poachers at last catching game

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of poachers
tag is the playground game where one child chases and catches the others

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps company with poachers finally gets caught taking game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is not the verb but the plural of doe: a stag keeps company with female deer. 'game' looks like hunted animals, but 'catching game' is the children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, which runs with the hinds or does of its herd.

clue.text: Printer malfunctioning with bug — that's troubling

indicators.note: a malfunctioning machine produces garbled output, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office printer going wrong because of a software bug is a worrying thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb is to disturb or worry someone, so something perturbing is unsettling or worrying.

clue.text: Beastly group with info on unfinished work

indicators.note: in an across clue, info on the work means the info comes after it
unfinished means the word for work loses its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work, a task
data is information, info

explanation.surface: A dreadful band hands over information about a job left half done.
explanation.walkthrough: CHORE without its end gives CHOR, followed by DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Chordata is the zoological phylum of animals with a notochord, including all vertebrates: a group of beasts.

clue.text: Helmsman in endless river redirected missile

indicators.note: sent in the opposite direction, so the whole string is read backwards
the helmsman sits inside the river

parts.note: the River Tees in north-east England, minus its last letter
the cox steers a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A rowing cox on a river has had to change course because of a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England; a cox steers a rowing eight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exocet is a French-built anti-ship missile, famous from its use in the Falklands War.

clue.text: I should follow lover, once helping to find forgiveness

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed behind the former lover

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
I is the Roman numeral one
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they ought to go back to their ex, and helping them would be a way of being forgiven.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoneration is the clearing of blame, a release from guilt close in sense to pardon.

clue.text: Gorilla sat uneasily, seeing swamp predators

indicators.note: sitting uneasily means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gorilla shifts nervously because it has spotted dangerous animals in the marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Alligators are large reptiles that hunt in the swamps and marshes of the southern United States and China.

clue.text: Lacking refinement in lament that ignores Unknown Soldier?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: lament gives ELEGY, before the Y goes
Y, a mathematical unknown, removed from the lament
a soldier is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A clumsy line in a lament for the Unknown Soldier, the anonymous war dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letters make 'Unknown Soldier' look like the war memorial; split apart, Unknown is Y and Soldier is ANT, a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means graceless or clumsy, the opposite of refined or polished.

clue.text: Atmosphere's raised about bodily form, losing my patients here?

indicators.note: about means the turned atmosphere letters go around the rest
raised means the letters are turned upwards, read from bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: air is atmosphere, and the 's adds an S: AIRS

indicators.note: losing means the word my is taken out of the word for bodily form

parts.note: anatomy is the structure of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried thought: the air's gone up around my body, and I'm losing my patients?
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIRS into SRIA; ANATOMY 'losing' MY is ANATO, and SRIA goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria are institutions where convalescent or chronically ill people stay for treatment, so patients are found there.

clue.text: John: name for Scots lad

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: John is apparently what they call a boy in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name, but it is the American slang word for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Loon (or loun) is a Scots and northern dialect word for a boy or youth.

clue.text: Clubs held by United — but not now?

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: united means made one
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A football club that Manchester United used to own but no longer does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football team, but means made into ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some former time, so it describes something true formerly but not at present.

clue.text: Ground where one welcomes island leader

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the island goes inside
something ground is crushed and broken up, so these letters are re-formed

parts.note: taken as written
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A patch of land where someone greets the chief of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun meaning land, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was Supreme Allied Commander in Europe and later US President, a leader in war and peace.

clue.text: His law affected India's lingua franca

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so these letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ruler's legislation shaped the common language of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India's' points to the country, but it only supplies I; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is the Bantu language used as a common trading tongue across East Africa.

clue.text: Ambassador in sight finding guillotine

indicators.note: the ambassador is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a bead is the front sight on a gun barrel, as in drawing a bead on
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat catches sight of an executioner's blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To guillotine someone is to cut off their head, which is what behead means.

clue.text: Copy made where nothing replaces end of simple song?

indicators.note: replaces means the nothing letter takes the place of another letter in the song
end of points to the final letter of the song word as the one swapped out

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A question about plagiarism: is it copying if you change the last note of a tune?
explanation.walkthrough: DITTY has its end letter Y replaced by O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, a duplicate, so it stands for a copy.

clue.text: West Indian hostile to assassin casing area

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: a casing wraps around its contents, so the area sits inside

parts.note: a gun is a hired killer, as in gunman
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A Caribbean man who opposes a hitman staking out a neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island in the West Indies, so a native of it is an Antiguan.

clue.text: Bottled spirits and dope given to Latin couple

parts.note: gen and dope both mean inside information
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Bottles of liquor and drugs handed to a pair of Latin speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled spirits' reads as liquor but means the genies of folklore that live in lamps or bottles. 'dope' is information, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie or genius, the magical spirits famously trapped in bottles and lamps.

clue.text: More sneaky one hidden by small duck, almost there

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the teal is a small duck

indicators.note: something hidden by another is enclosed inside it
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: there, missing its last letter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone crouching behind a little duck has nearly got there, being sneakier than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the Roman numeral I, tucked inside the shortened word, which follows the small duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means acting covertly so as not to be seen, which is to be sneaky; the comparative form matches.

clue.text: Leaves to create drink regularly offered in the bar

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A bartender regularly serves a drink made by steeping leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' and 'bar' suggest something alcoholic, but the leaves are what you brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the dried leaves of the tea plant, infused in hot water to make the drink.

clue.text: Most important having rook in such dark films?

indicators.note: having means taking on something extra, here added at the end

parts.note: number one, NO 1, is the most important
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: The best-known films in this genre feature a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that NOIR is the genre name rather than a plural noun, as in film noir.
explanation.definitionFit: Noir is short for film noir, the shadowy black-and-white crime-film genre known for its bleak mood.

clue.text: Despotic writer appears before Italian heretic

indicators.note: appearing before means coming first, so these parts are placed in order

parts.note: an author is a writer
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
Arians followed Arius, whose teaching the early Church condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A tyrannical author turns up ahead of an Italian dissenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Authoritarian means demanding strict obedience to authority, characteristic of a tyrant or dictator.
